title: What are the Core Web Vitals metrics included in Google's assessment, and what do they measure?
content:
Q: What are the Core Web Vitals metrics included in Google's assessment, and what do they measure?
A: Google's Core Web Vitals Assessment includes the following metrics:

- **Largest Contentful Paint (LCP):** An indication of a site's loading time, specifically how long it takes for the largest content element in the site's viewport to load.
- **Interaction to Next Paint (INP):** An assessment of your site's responsiveness to all click, tap, and keyboard interactions that occur throughout each visit on every page. The final INP value is the longest interaction observed.
- **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS):** A measurement of unexpected movements of elements that change the layout of the page.

title: How can I adjust my live stream settings in OBS Studio to ensure optimal performance with Wix Video?
content:
Q: How can I adjust my live stream settings in OBS Studio to ensure optimal performance with Wix Video?
A: To adjust your live stream settings in OBS Studio for optimal performance with Wix Video, follow these steps:

1. Open the OBS Studio Encoder on your computer.
2. Click **Settings** on the bottom right.
3. Select the **Output** tab to change the codec, audio, and video bitrates.
4. Select the **Video** tab to change the video resolution.

Make sure you don't exceed the following settings:
- **Video Resolution:** 720p (1280x720)
- **Codec:** x264
- **Video bitrate:** ~2500 kbps
- **Audio bitrate:** AAC 44.1kHz ~128kbps

**Important:** The output needs to be set to 'Simple'. If it is set to 'Advanced', it can cause issues with the live stream.

**Tip:** If your internet bandwidth is less than 3000 kb/s, reduce the video and audio bitrates so that the sum fits your bandwidth. A general rule is to have double the bandwidth for your target bitrate to help ensure you maintain your bandwidth during internet fluctuations.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/live-stream-settings-resolution-bitrates-and-codecs

title: How can I ensure my logo design looks good in all sizes according to Wix's best practices?
content:
Q: How can I ensure my logo design looks good in all sizes according to Wix's best practices?
A: To ensure your logo design looks good in all sizes, follow these tips:

- Make sure that your logo looks good in all sizes, from large to small. Try to zoom out or check it in a small size like it normally appears on your brand materials, and check that everything is clear, and the text is readable.
- Avoid overlapping text when designing your logo, as the texts blend into one color and are unreadable in some files. This happens in the following file types:
  
  + **Standard logo files:** Black on Transparent, Black on White, White on Black and White on Transparent.
  + **Resizable vector files:** Black and White.

Additionally, ensure that the elements contrast against their background to prevent them from looking pixelated in small sizes. Be cautious with extremely thin font weights or thin-lined icons and shapes, as they can look blurred or even invisible in small sizes.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-logo-best-practices-for-logo-design

title: What are the requirements for uploading a photo ID for Wix Payments verification?
content:
Q: What are the requirements for uploading a photo ID for Wix Payments verification?
A: Your photo ID must meet the following requirements:

* Your photo ID can be a passport, driver's license or a government issued ID card
* Your photo ID must be active and non-expired
* The photo must be in color
* Your ID must show all 4 borders and corners
* The ID must not have information blocked or blacked out
* The ID must be straightened, not angled or rotated
* The ID must not be blurry, overexposed or copied from another source (e.g. screenshot)
* Your first, middle and last name in your Wix Payments account must match those of your ID
* Your birth date in your Wix Payments account must match that of your ID
* For passports with a Machine-Readable Zone (MRZ), the MRZ must be visible.
* For driver's licenses or government issue ID cards, send a separate file for each side
* Documents must be sent in one of the following: HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, PNG
* The maximum file size is 10 MB
* The minimum file size is 1 KB for PDF, 100 KB for other formats

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/guidelines-for-uploading-documentation-for-wix-payments

Here, you can use the **Top stats** overview to find out what products are selling best, what items are converting the most, and what services are being booked most often. Depending on the Wix apps you have installed, you'll see personalized metrics such as:

- **Top selling items:** Discover which of your products, tickets, services, and subscriptions are most popular.
- **Top converting products (Wix Stores):** See which products convert well and identify the products that could convert better.
- **Top selling variants (Wix Stores):** Discover which product variants (e.g., size L, color brown) are selling the most.
- **Most abandoned products (Wix Stores):** Understand which products visitors add to their cart but don't end up purchasing.
- **Most booked services (Wix Bookings):** Discover which services were booked the most.
- **Top paying subscriptions (Wix Pricing Plans):** See which subscriptions bring you the most revenue.
- **Top selling events (Wix Events):** Discover which events bring you the most revenue and see the total tickets sold for each event.
- **Top selling dishes (Wix Restaurants):** See your top selling dishes and find out what customers ordered the most.

These metrics vary depending on your business app. For example, if you've installed Wix Events, you will see 'Tickets sold' as a top stat.

A: To view the predicted occupancy for your classes in Wix Analytics, follow these steps:

2. Choose the **Classes** view at the top right according to your service type.
3. In the **Predicted occupancy** section, click the drop-down to show the predicted occupancy for the **next week** (7 days starting next Sunday) or the **next 7 days** (7 days starting tomorrow).
4. The progress bar will show you the following details:
   - **Spots filled/Confirmed appointments:** This is the number of already booked sessions.
   - **Predicted:** This is the number of additional bookings that are likely to be made based on the confirmed bookings from the previous 3-4 weeks.
   - **Available:** This is the number of spots left open, calculated as the total capacity minus predicted occupancy.

**Note:** Predicted occupancy is the sum of confirmed spots that you already have for the next week/next 7 days and the predicted spots. The predicted numbers rely on the number of confirmed bookings in the past 3-4 weeks.

Changing a TTL value does not speed up the time it takes for a DNS record to propagate. It only changes the amount of time before your computer is forced to make a new DNS request.

title: Why does a charge appear twice on my customer's bank statement, and what should be done if it doesn't disappear?
content:
Q: Why does a charge appear twice on my customer's bank statement, and what should be done if it doesn't disappear?
A: Sometimes a charge may appear to have been made twice on your customer's bank statement. This does not mean that your customer makes two payments. When paying for goods or services by credit card, a credit card company may authorize the card for the amount due before the actual funds are taken. The authorization (pending charge) appears on your customer's bank statement and may look like a charge, however, no funds are actually taken at that time. The authorization should disappear from online bank statements within a month. If the authorization does not disappear, please advise your customer to contact their bank for further information.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/understanding-double-charges-on-your-customers-bank-statements

title: How can I ensure that using Google Fonts on my Wix site complies with the GDPR?
content:
Q: How can I ensure that using Google Fonts on my Wix site complies with the GDPR?
A: In a recent decision, a regional court in Munich ruled that the “dynamic use” of Google Fonts violates the EU GDPR. This is due to the fact that your visitor's IP address could be transmitted to Google's servers in the United States. Wix has developed an in-house solution to remedy this issue. Google Fonts are now hosted locally within Wix. This means that no IP data is transmitted from the EU to Google's servers in the United States. 

**Note**: If you add fonts to your site using alternative methods such as custom embeds, custom elements or iframes, they may contain Google Fonts and we cannot guarantee that these will be hosted locally.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/faqs-google-wix-and-the-gdpr

title: How can I view the revenue from different types of subscriptions over the last 12 months in Wix Analytics?
content:
Q: How can I view the revenue from different types of subscriptions over the last 12 months in Wix Analytics?
A: To view the revenue from different types of subscriptions over the last 12 months in Wix Analytics, go to the **Revenue over the last 12 months** section. This section displays a graph of the total revenue you've received from different types of subscriptions on your site over the last 12 months. You can view revenue for all plans together or click the **All plans** drop-down to filter by a specific plan. The 4 revenue types include:

* **One-time:** Revenue from subscriptions that aren’t recurring (the client pays only once).
* **First recurring:** Revenue from the first payment of a recurring subscription.
* **Recurring:** Revenue from recurring payments (excluding first payment).
* **Expected recurring:** This metric calculates all the payments that you should get from existing subscriptions this month, but have not yet received.

**Important:** This isn’t a prediction based on historical sales, rather a projection of upcoming payments for existing subscriptions. This metric does not include new subscriptions that may be purchased in the future (during this month), and does not consider any possible cancellations.

title: What are the supported file types and size limits for uploading images to a Wix site?
content:
Q: What are the supported file types and size limits for uploading images to a Wix site?
A: For site images, Wix supports the following file types: JPG, PNG, GIF, JPEG, JPE, JFIF, BMP, HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, TIF, WEBP, JPEG 2000, and RAW. The supported JPEG 2000 file formats include .jp2, .jpg2, .j2k, .jpf, .jpm, .j2c, .jpc, .jpx, and the supported RAW file formats include .arw, .srw, .nef, .cr2, .cr3, .crw, .rwl, .rw2, .raw, .raf, .pef, .orf, .mrw, .dng, .sr2, .srf, .kdc, .k25, .dcr, .x3f, .erf, .3fr. Animated WEBP images are currently not supported and convert to static images.

The file size limits for images are 25MB, and for GIFs, it is 15MB.

For background images, the supported file types are JPG, PNG, GIF, JPEG, JPE, JFIF, BMP, HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, TIF, and WEBP, with a recommended file size of at least 3000 x 3000px.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-media-supported-media-file-types-and-file-sizes

title: How can I enable Single Sign-On (SSO) login for my organization using Wix?
content:
Q: How can I enable Single Sign-On (SSO) login for my organization using Wix?
A: Prerequisites: Ensure you have completed the setup of your Identity Provider (IdP) settings and have the necessary information such as Client ID, Client Secret, and Config URL.

To enable SSO login and set it as required:

1. Click the **Enable SSO** toggle to enable or disable SSO login:
   * **Enabled:** Your users can sign in to their Wix account using SSO or other methods such as an email address and password.
   * **Disabled:** Your users cannot sign in using SSO. They can still sign in using other methods.
2. Click the **Set SSO as required** toggle to choose whether or not you want to require your users to sign in by SSO.
   * **Enabled:** Users can only sign in with SSO. They cannot sign in using other methods such as an email and password. Account owners can still sign in using other methods.
   * **Disabled:** Users can sign in using SSO or other methods.

**Important:** Wix recommends that you manually test your SSO settings before setting SSO as required.

3. Click **Save Changes**.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-enterprise-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso-login
